title: Who Has the Right to Explain an Old Object?
title_ja: 古い文化財を説明する権利は誰にあるか

source_links.title: ICOM: Code of Ethics for Museums

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: A city museum displays a beautifully decorated wooden object that was collected from a distant community many decades ago.
sentences.ja: 市の博物館は何十年も前に遠くの地域から集められた美しく装飾された木製品を展示します。

sentences.en: The label explains its age, materials, and possible original function, using information gathered by researchers.
sentences.ja: 説明札には研究者が集めた情報を使い、年代、素材、元の用途の可能性が記されています。

sentences.en: Visitors admire the craftsmanship, but a representative from the community asks why no one consulted its members when writing the label.
sentences.ja: 来館者は細工を称賛しますが、地域の代表者は札を書くときなぜ住民に相談しなかったのか尋ねます。

sentences.en: However, the museum has treated the object mainly as a historical artifact while the community still regards it as part of a living cultural practice.
sentences.ja: しかし博物館はそれを歴史的遺物とみなし、地域社会はいまも生きた文化的実践の一部と考えています。

sentences.en: The disagreement is not simply about translating a few words on a wall; it concerns who can interpret cultural meaning.
sentences.ja: 意見の違いは壁の数語の翻訳だけでなく、文化的な意味を誰が解釈できるかに関わります。

sentences.en: An apparently neutral description may leave out relationships and responsibilities that matter to people connected with the object.
sentences.ja: 中立に見える説明でも、物品に関わる人々に重要な関係や責任が省かれることがあります。

sentences.en: The museum director invites several community members to discuss how the collection should be presented to visitors.
sentences.ja: 館長は地域の住民を招き、収集物をどう来館者へ示すか話し合います。

sentences.en: For example, some participants want the label to explain that the object was used during gatherings, not merely in private decoration.
sentences.ja: 例えば物品が私的な装飾だけでなく集まりで使われたと説明してほしい参加者もいます。

sentences.en: Others argue that certain information should not be publicly displayed because it is shared only under particular cultural conditions.
sentences.ja: 別の人は特定の文化的条件の下でのみ伝えられる情報は公開すべきでないと主張します。

sentences.en: The discussion reveals that a community is not a single person with a single opinion about its heritage.
sentences.ja: 話し合いは地域社会が遺産について一つの意見しか持たない一人の人間ではないことを示します。

sentences.en: Museum staff must listen to different voices without assuming that whichever speaker talks most confidently represents everyone.
sentences.ja: 職員は最も自信を持って話す人が全員を代表すると決めつけず、複数の声を聞かなければなりません。

sentences.en: Meaningful consultation is more demanding than asking someone to approve a description after every important decision has already been made.
sentences.ja: 意味ある協議は重要な決定の後に説明文の承認を求めるより難しいものです。

sentences.en: Professional museum ethics emphasize responsible stewardship and respectful relationships with communities connected to collections.
sentences.ja: 博物館の専門倫理は責任ある管理と収蔵品に関係する地域社会との敬意ある関係を重視します。

sentences.en: In addition, an object may have been acquired under historical circumstances that would be judged differently today.
sentences.ja: さらに物品は今日なら異なる評価を受ける歴史的事情の下で取得されたかもしれません。

sentences.en: Researchers should examine available records of acquisition rather than presume that every item entered a collection in the same way.
sentences.ja: 研究者はすべての品が同じ方法で収蔵されたと決めつけず、利用可能な取得記録を調べるべきです。

sentences.en: A dispute about an object's future may involve questions of law, cultural authority, conservation, and the conditions under which it was transferred.
sentences.ja: 物品の将来をめぐる論争には法律、文化的権限、保存、移転条件が関わる場合があります。

sentences.en: A short description cannot resolve all of these questions, but it can acknowledge that important uncertainties remain.
sentences.ja: 短い説明文でこれらすべては解決できませんが、重要な不確実さが残ることを認められます。

sentences.en: Honest labels distinguish established historical facts from interpretations that are still being discussed.
sentences.ja: 誠実な説明札は確認された歴史事実とまだ議論中の解釈を区別します。

sentences.en: The museum proposes an updated exhibition in which visitors can encounter several explanations rather than one supposedly final account.
sentences.ja: 博物館は来館者が唯一の最終説明でなく複数の説明に出会える新展示を提案します。

sentences.en: Community contributors can describe the meanings they wish to share while museum researchers explain what documentary evidence supports.
sentences.ja: 地域の協力者は共有したい意味を説明し、研究者は資料が支える内容を説明できます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, simply placing two quotations side by side would not settle difficult questions about permission or ownership.
sentences.ja: それでも二つの引用を並べるだけでは許可や所有をめぐる難しい問題は解決しません。

sentences.en: The museum establishes a continuing process for consultation and records which concerns it has addressed and which remain open.
sentences.ja: 博物館は継続的な協議の仕組みを作り、対応した懸念と未解決の懸念を記録します。

sentences.en: Its goal is not to create the impression that every disagreement has vanished, but to make the decisions behind the exhibition visible.
sentences.ja: 目標はすべての不一致が消えた印象を作るのでなく、展示の背後の意思決定を見える形にすることです。

sentences.en: Respectful interpretation grows from shared inquiry rather than the assumption that preserving an object gives one institution the final word.
sentences.ja: 敬意ある解釈は、保存している組織に最終的な発言権があるという思い込みでなく共同の探究から生まれます。

questions.prompt: What is the central argument of the passage?
options: Museums should consider multiple community voices, historical evidence, and ethical responsibility when interpreting objects.
Museum labels should never contain history.
Every community has one identical opinion.
Researchers alone should make all cultural decisions.
questions.explanation_ja: 多様な声と倫理に配慮した解釈が主題です。

questions.prompt: What does the original museum label emphasize?
options: A complete record of community opinions.
The object's age, materials, and possible function.
The price of every visitor's ticket.
questions.explanation_ja: 年代や素材、用途の推定です。

questions.prompt: Why does the community representative question the label?
options: The object has never been studied.
Living cultural meanings may be missing from the museum's account.
Every label must be extremely long.
questions.explanation_ja: 生きた文化の意味が欠けている可能性があるためです。

questions.prompt: What do some participants want visitors to understand?
options: Every object was made in a factory.
All artifacts have the same function.
The object was used in gatherings rather than only for decoration.
questions.explanation_ja: 集まりでの使用を伝えたいと述べます。

questions.prompt: Why should staff listen beyond the most confident speaker?
options: A community can contain different views and experiences.
Only one person can know history.
questions.explanation_ja: 地域内にもさまざまな意見があるためです。

questions.prompt: What should researchers examine about acquisition?
options: Records showing how the object entered the collection.
Only the lighting of the gallery.
The sale of all museum objects.
A new form of wooden decoration.
Responsible care and management of something entrusted to an institution.
The price of conserving one painting.
questions.explanation_ja: stewardshipは責任ある保管・管理です。

questions.prompt: Why is a revised label alone insufficient?
options: Every community wants an identical label.
Ownership and permission may require ongoing examination and decisions.
questions.explanation_ja: 所有や許可の問題は別に残り得るためです。

questions.prompt: What process does the museum establish?
options: Continuing consultation and a record of unresolved concerns.
questions.explanation_ja: 継続的な協議と懸念の記録です。

questions.prompt: What is implied by the final sentence?
options: Holding an object does not automatically give a museum exclusive authority over its meaning.
Every disagreement must disappear before a museum opens.
questions.explanation_ja: 物品の保管と意味の独占は別だという結論です。
